title: Foreign investors show early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian equities, with analysts highlighting big banks and select sectors.
text: Foreign investors show early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian equities, with analysts highlighting big banks and select sectors. Foreign investors are showing early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian stocks, with net buying concentrated in large-cap banks during the week of August 31 to September 4, 2026. In that period, foreign net purchases reached Rp1.85–2.3 trillion, led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, which together recorded over Rp3.19 trillion of net foreign buying in the regular market. LQ45 outflows have declined sharply from over Rp15 trillion in June to under Rp2 trillion in August, and the number of LQ45 stocks with outflows fell to 27 from 36 in June. Analysts caution this is not yet a structural trend reversal, as year-to-date foreign outflows remain around US$3.94 billion, and sustainability depends on Federal Reserve policy, rupiah stability, and earnings growth. Potential rotation targets include commodity stocks ANTM, AMMN, and INCO, as well as consumer and industrial names TLKM, ASII, INDF, and UNTR, with advisors recommending accumulation on weakness.

title: PT Astra International Tbk’s car sales rise 10% YoY, analyst recommends buying the stock
text: PT Astra International Tbk’s car sales rise 10% YoY, analyst recommends buying the stock The article discusses the outlook for PT Astra International Tbk’s automotive segment, noting a 10% year‑on‑year increase in car sales to 222,371 units in the first half of 2026. This growth kept Astra’s domestic market share above 50% while national car sales grew 16% to 436,567 units, and the analyst highlighted spill‑over benefits to its financing, insurance, components and after‑sales businesses. However, the analyst warned that slower growth relative to the market, competition from electric and hybrid manufacturers, high interest rates, and weaker contributions from United Tractors’ heavy‑equipment and mining operations could moderate profit expansion. The recommendation is a buy (or buy on weakness) with technical targets of breaking the Rp5,000 resistance and moving toward Rp5,400‑Rp5,600, and ultimately Rp6,000‑Rp6,100 per share.

title: Rupiah Weakening Raises Pressure on ASII While PT Selamat Sempurna Tbk Gains from Export‑Dollar Exposure
text: Rupiah Weakening Raises Pressure on ASII While PT Selamat Sempurna Tbk Gains from Export‑Dollar Exposure The rupiah slipped to Rp 18,049 per US$ on 4 June 2026, a 0.46% daily decline and a 7.91% depreciation since the start of 2026, heightening cost concerns for automotive issuers dependent on imported components. ASII, described as a diversified automotive group, is judged resilient with analysts keeping a long‑term buy call and a target price of Rp 7,100, while short‑term price is projected around Rp 5,500‑5,800. PT Selamat Sempurna Tbk, whose about 65% of sales are export‑priced in dollars and 60% of raw‑material costs are dollar‑denominated, benefits from natural hedging that offsets higher import costs, reporting no material negative impact on operations. Companies with higher import reliance such as IMAS and ASII are seen as more exposed to the currency weakness, though ASII’s scale and diversification moderate the risk.

title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports first‑half 2026 capex of Rp 17 trillion, driven by subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR).
text: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports first‑half 2026 capex of Rp 17 trillion, driven by subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR). PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) disclosed that it has realized approximately Rp 17 trillion of capital expenditure in the first half of 2026, out of a total planned capex of Rp 35‑36 trillion for the year. The majority of the spending was incurred by its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), primarily for the acquisition of the Arafura Surya Alam gold mine and for routine purchases of heavy equipment for its mining contractor business. Astra indicated that the remaining capex budget will be allocated in a disciplined manner to support productivity and profit growth through 2027. The company said it will continue periodic evaluations to ensure the capex contributes optimally to earnings growth.

title: BEI announces KOMPAS100 index rebalancing, removing BREN, HMSP and six others while adding BNBR, COIN and seven new constituents
text: BEI announces KOMPAS100 index rebalancing, removing BREN, HMSP and six others while adding BNBR, COIN and seven new constituents The Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) officially announced a rebalancing of the KOMPAS100 index for the period August 2026 to January 2027. Effective 3 August 2026, nine stocks – PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN), PT Bank BTPN Syariah Tbk (BTPS), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), PT MD Pictures Tbk (FILM), PT HM Sampoerna Tbk (HMSP), PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa Tbk (INTP), PT Dayamitra Telekomunikasi Tbk (MTEL), PT Industri Jamu dan Farmasi Sido Muncul Tbk (SIDO) and PT Transcoal Pacific Tbk (TCPI) – are removed from the index. They are replaced by nine new constituents – PT BFI Finance Indonesia Tbk (BFIN), PT Astrindo Nusantara Infrastruktur Tbk (BIPI), PT Bakrie & Brothers Tbk (BNBR), PT Indokripto Koin Semesta Tbk (COIN), PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (EMAS), PT Gudang Garam Tbk (GGRM), PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP), PT Sanurhasta Mitra Tbk (MINA) and PT RMK Energy Tbk (RMKE). The revised composition will be used for index calculation from 3 August to 30 October 2026, reflecting the index’s mandate to include stocks with high liquidity, sound fundamentals and sufficient market capitalization. Other large‑cap issuers such as BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, TLKM, ASII, AMMN, BRIS, GOTO and TPIA remain in the index.

title: PT Astra International Tbk reports H1 2026 revenue of Rp 157.9 trillion and net profit of Rp 12.5 trillion
text: PT Astra International Tbk reports H1 2026 revenue of Rp 157.9 trillion and net profit of Rp 12.5 trillion PT Astra International Tbk posted consolidated net revenue of Rp 157.9 trillion and net profit of Rp 12.5 trillion for the first half of 2026. Revenue fell 3% YoY and net profit declined 19% while adjusted net profit (excluding non‑recurring items) dropped 7% to Rp 14.9 trillion, with Rp 2.4 trillion of non‑recurring items mainly fair‑value adjustments and impairment. The lower contribution from the mining solutions and heavy‑equipment business was offset by gains in automotive and financial‑services segments, and net debt rose to Rp 6 trillion (excluding financial‑services subsidiaries) as the group completed the acquisition of PT Arafura Surya Alam and executed share‑buyback and working‑capital actions. PT Astra International Tbk approved a new share‑buyback program of up to Rp 8 trillion for the next 12 months, and United Tractors announced its own buyback of up to Rp 2 trillion for three months, adding to the combined Rp 7.4 trillion buyback completed through June 2026. The company reaffirmed its new corporate strategy focused on automotive, financial services, and mining‑solution businesses amid ongoing global uncertainty.

title: Astra International completes Rp810.7 billion share buyback and plans up to Rp8 trillion repurchase
text: Astra International completes Rp810.7 billion share buyback and plans up to Rp8 trillion repurchase Astra International (ASII) completed a share buyback of Rp810.7 billion, absorbing 153.42 million shares at an average price of Rp5,283 per share. text: ASII's automotive segment grows 9% to Rp5.9 trillion in 1H26, driven by Toyota and Daihatsu sales ASII's automotive segment grew 9% to Rp5.9 trillion in the first half of 2026, driven by new car sales and a 23% rise in net profit from its component division to Rp921 billion. title: PT Astra International Tbk shifts strategy to prioritize TSR and announces up to Rp8 trillion buyback
text: PT Astra International Tbk shifts strategy to prioritize TSR and announces up to Rp8 trillion buyback PT Astra International Tbk said it is refocusing its strategy on value creation and a target total shareholder return (TSR) in the low‑teens, well above its historical average of about 6% per year for 2015‑2025. The group plans to fund the shift with a stable 5‑6% dividend yield, a 45‑50% payout ratio and a buyback program backed by roughly Rp8 trillion of cash earmarked for the next 12 months. Its three core businesses—automotive, financial services and heavy‑equipment/mining solutions—account for about 90% of 2025 net profit, with the automotive segment aiming to maintain roughly 50% market share in four‑wheel vehicles while expanding its two‑wheel and used‑car offerings. CGS International Sekuritas Indonesia analyst Handy Noverdanius reaffirmed an “add” rating on ASII with a target price of Rp6,850, citing the strategic shift and potential catalysts such as stronger consumer purchasing power and new automotive incentives.

title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports Rp17 trillion capex in H1 2026, targeting Rp36 trillion total for the year.
text: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports Rp17 trillion capex in H1 2026, targeting Rp36 trillion total for the year. PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) has realized Rp17 trillion of capital expenditure in the first half of 2026, which is almost half of its planned Rp36 trillion capex for the year. The bulk of the spending was driven by its mining business, primarily through its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), covering gold and other mineral operations. The remainder of the capex consists of routine investments such as heavy‑equipment purchases for mining contractors. Astra expects to allocate the remaining roughly Rp19 trillion in the second half of 2026 in a more disciplined manner to support future growth.

title: PT Astra International Tbk reports 19% drop in first‑half 2026 net profit as mining and heavy‑equipment business pressures earnings
text: PT Astra International Tbk reports 19% drop in first‑half 2026 net profit as mining and heavy‑equipment business pressures earnings PT Astra International Tbk, a multi‑sector holding owned by Jardine Cycle & Carriage Limited, said its consolidated net profit fell 19% year‑on‑year to Rp12.53 trillion in the first half of 2026. The decline was driven by a 46% drop in the mining‑solution and heavy‑equipment segment, which posted Rp2.7 trillion profit amid weak sales at the Martabe gold mine and reduced national coal quotas. By contrast, the automotive and financial‑services segments grew, delivering Rp5.91 trillion (up 9%) and Rp4.64 trillion (up 6%) respectively, while other segments contributed Rp1.6 trillion and the company recorded a Rp2.35 trillion investment impairment. Astra reaffirmed its new corporate strategy launched in Q2, focusing on the three core businesses, disciplined capital allocation, dividend, share buyback and leadership transformation.

The day's biggest index contributors were DCII, CASA and BMRI, while TLKM, BREN and ASII weighed on the market; foreign investors recorded net sells of IDR 491.89 billion in the regular market and IDR 820.67 billion across all markets. SUNI secured two new contracts worth a combined IDR 106.29 billion, bringing its contract value to about 32.78% of first‑half 2026 sales despite a 25.99% drop in sales and a 35.60% decline in profit. INET launched the NewConnext digital service and reported net revenue of IDR 383.60 billion, up sharply from IDR 12.10 billion, with outsourcing contributing 86.79% of revenue. PT Midi Utama Indonesia Tbk posted first‑half net revenue of IDR 11.25 trillion (up 8.45%) and profit of IDR 485.97 billion (up 24.44%), expanded to 2,662 stores and plans to open about 200 new outlets in 2026 with capex of IDR 1.50 trillion.

title: PT Astra International Tbk announces Rp 8 trillion share buyback, joining PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk in jumbo repurchase programs
text: PT Astra International Tbk announces Rp 8 trillion share buyback, joining PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk in jumbo repurchase programs PT Astra International Tbk plans a share buyback of about Rp 8 trillion using internal funds. PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk announced a buyback program of roughly Rp 4 trillion, while PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk set a maximum buyback size of Rp 500 billion. title: Prospects and Recommendations for LQ45 Constituents After First‑Half 2026 Earnings
text: Prospects and Recommendations for LQ45 Constituents After First‑Half 2026 Earnings The article reviews the earnings released by LQ45 constituents for the first half of 2026 and evaluates their stock prospects. Of the 29 companies that have reported, most posted revenue and profit growth, while six showed profit declines, with banking stocks BMRI and BBCA highlighted for solid performance—BMRI posted a 24.4% YoY profit increase and BBCA maintained stable earnings and a credit portfolio exceeding Rp1 trillion. Conversely, ICBP’s profit fell 33% due to currency losses and UNTR faced operational pressure; consumer‑goods firm UNVR’s gross profit margin slipped to 44.9% in Q2 2026, and automotive group ASII reported net profit of Rp6.7 trillion, down 22.14% YoY. Analysts from Kiwoom Securities and Ajaib Securities note that despite a positive overall outlook for LQ45, selective strength and macro‑headwinds such as a 100‑basis‑point rate hike to 5.75% and a PMI contraction to 46.9 keep the outlook mixed.

title: Analyst projects continued positive performance for PT Astra International Tbk to 2026 and issues a buy‑on‑weakness recommendation
text: Analyst projects continued positive performance for PT Astra International Tbk to 2026 and issues a buy‑on‑weakness recommendation The article discusses an analyst’s outlook that PT Astra International Tbk will maintain a positive performance trajectory through the end of 2026. It cites first‑half‑2026 vehicle sales of 222,371 units, a 10 % year‑on‑year increase, while the national market grew 16 % to 436,567 units, allowing Astra to keep a market share above 50 %. The analyst notes that Astra’s integrated businesses—including financing, insurance, components, after‑sales services and its heavy‑equipment arm United Tractors—provide cross‑segment support, though higher interest rates, a weaker rupiah and competitive pressure from electric and hybrid vehicles pose risks. Technically, the stock faces resistance at Rp 5,000 and, if broken with strong volume, the target range is Rp 5,400‑5,600 with a longer‑term aim of Rp 6,000‑6,100. The analyst recommends a buy‑on‑weakness strategy for ASII shares.

title: Analysts project stronger H2 2026 performance for PT Astra International Tbk on diversified revenue base
text: Analysts project stronger H2 2026 performance for PT Astra International Tbk on diversified revenue base The article assesses PT Astra International Tbk’s outlook, noting that its diversified revenue base—particularly automotive, financial services, and mining—should support stronger results in the second half of 2026. Ciptadana Sekuritas Asia reports H1 2026 revenue of IDR 157.9 trillion (‑3% YoY) and net profit of IDR 12.5 trillion (‑19.2% YoY), but Q2 2026 net profit rose 14.2% QoQ to IDR 6.7 trillion driven by a 5.9% YoY increase in automotive revenue to IDR 66.1 trillion and a 10% YoY rise in vehicle sales to 222,000 units, preserving a 51% market share. The firm forecasts full‑year 2026 revenue of IDR 319.35 trillion and net profit of IDR 31.40 trillion, with EPS growth of 28.4% projected for FY26‑28, while BRI Danareksa and UBS analysts also keep buy recommendations, setting target prices of IDR 6,400, 7,380 and 6,850 per share. Risks highlighted include a possible slowdown in automotive demand, a weaker rupiah and high interest rates, whereas a planned IDR 8 trillion share buyback, a 45‑50% dividend payout and a low‑teens total shareholder return are cited as positive catalysts. PT Astra Sedaya Finance, Astra’s financing subsidiary, is noted for a 10% YoY increase in new consumer financing to IDR 61.8 trillion, contributing to the stable earnings outlook.

title: United Tractors reports Rp58.3 trillion revenue for H1 2026, down 15% YoY
text: United Tractors reports Rp58.3 trillion revenue for H1 2026, down 15% YoY United Tractors, a subsidiary of PT Astra International Tbk, posted net revenue of Rp58.3 trillion in the first half of 2026, a 15% year‑on‑year decline from Rp68.5 trillion. The decline was driven by lower gold sales from its subsidiary PT Agincourt Resources after a temporary shutdown of the Martabe gold mine and weaker performance in the heavy‑equipment and thermal‑coal mining segments due to reduced national coal allocation. Net profit excluding non‑recurring items fell 48% to Rp4.3 trillion, while non‑recurring losses totaled Rp3.3 trillion, and net debt rose to Rp9.4 trillion, giving a gearing ratio of 8.5% as of 30 June 2026. Heavy‑equipment revenue fell 28% to Rp15.0 trillion as Komatsu equipment sales slipped 27% to 1,994 units, though parts and service revenue edged up to Rp5.5 trillion. The company noted that a stronger US‑dollar exchange rate and a share‑buyback programme partially offset the revenue shortfall.

title: PT Astra International Tbk approves up to Rp8 trillion share buyback
text: PT Astra International Tbk approves up to Rp8 trillion share buyback PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) received shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting on 17 July 2026 to conduct a share buyback program of up to Rp8 trillion. The buyback will be funded from internal cash, run for 12 months, and must not exceed 10 % of paid‑up capital while maintaining a free‑float of at least 15 %. In the current period III (16 Mar–15 Jun 2026) Astra repurchased 153.4 million shares for Rp810.7 billion, bringing total treasury holdings to 563.5 million shares since November 2025. Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia analyst Adrian Djie sees the program as financially neutral and recommends a short‑term buy with a target price of Rp5,300, while the stock closed at Rp5,100, down 23.88 % year‑to‑date.

title: PT Astra International Tbk Projects Rp115 Billion Additional Profit from Voluntary Tender Offer for PT Astra Otoparts Tbk Shares
text: PT Astra International Tbk Projects Rp115 Billion Additional Profit from Voluntary Tender Offer for PT Astra Otoparts Tbk Shares PT Astra International Tbk launched a voluntary tender offer (VTO) to acquire up to 238.44 million shares, or 4.94%, of its subsidiary PT Astra Otoparts Tbk at Rp3,600 per share, a premium to the Rp3,340 closing price on September 10, 2026. If fully subscribed, PT Astra International Tbk's ownership would rise to 84.95%, and the company projects an additional profit of approximately Rp115 billion from PT Astra Otoparts Tbk's estimated Rp2.2–2.3 trillion profit. PT Astra International Tbk has allocated Rp858 billion for the VTO and intends to maintain PT Astra Otoparts Tbk's public listing with a minimum 15% free float. PT Astra Otoparts Tbk reported first-half 2026 net profit of Rp1.15 trillion, up 22.6% year-on-year, with revenue rising 13.2% to Rp10.9 trillion, driven by both manufacturing and trading segments. The subsidiary's total assets reached Rp23.9 trillion and equity Rp17.2 trillion as of June 2026.

The automotive and financial services segments are projected to remain resilient throughout 2026. ASII reported a first-half 2026 net profit of Rp12.5 trillion on consolidated revenue of Rp157.9 trillion. Its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) posted a sharp 88.2% year-on-year decline in first-half net profit to Rp956.28 billion, with revenue falling 15% to Rp58.29 trillion, primarily due to lower gold sales at PT Agincourt Resources and weaker coal mining performance linked to a reduced national coal RKAB allocation. title: PT Astra International Tbk reports May 2026 vehicle sales of 38,768 units, capturing 56% market share
text: PT Astra International Tbk reports May 2026 vehicle sales of 38,768 units, capturing 56% market share PT Astra International Tbk reported selling 38,768 vehicles in May 2026, a 12.43% increase from 34,480 units a year earlier. The sales gave Astra a 56% share of the Indonesian passenger‑vehicle market in May, up from 52% in April. Sales were led by Toyota and Lexus models (24,983 units) followed by Daihatsu (11,140 units), Isuzu (2,570 units) and UD Trucks (75 units), while the LCGC segment fell to 6,836 units from 7,470 units in April. Despite a 7.15% monthly decline versus April’s 41,755 units, Astra’s performance outpaced the broader market, where Gaikindo reported a 14% YoY rise in four‑wheel vehicle sales.

title: Astra International focuses on automotive, financial services and mining segments while targeting recovery in Q2‑2026
text: Astra International focuses on automotive, financial services and mining segments while targeting recovery in Q2‑2026 PT Astra International Tbk reported a 6% YoY decline in Q1‑2026 consolidated revenue to Rp 78.7 trillion and a 16% YoY drop in net profit to Rp 5.9 trillion, with the Heavy Equipment, Mining, Construction & Energy (HEMCE) segment posting a 79% profit fall to Rp 408 billion. title: Astra International posts half‑year profit of Rp12.5 trillion and announces up to Rp8 trillion share buyback
text: Astra International posts half‑year profit of Rp12.5 trillion and announces up to Rp8 trillion share buyback Astra International reported half‑year 2026 net profit of Rp12.5 trillion, backed by consolidated revenue of Rp157.9 trillion. title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) Tightens Investment in Non-Core Businesses
text: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) Tightens Investment in Non-Core Businesses During Astra Media Day 2026 on 23 September, PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) said it will tighten its investment strategy for businesses outside its three core segments—automotive, financial services, and mining-solution & heavy-equipment operations. The company will evaluate its wider-business portfolio based on growth prospects, capital needs and contribution to the Astra ecosystem, continuing to invest in strategically important units, seeking partners for some, and re-assessing others. text: Foreign investors sell net Rp1.58 trillion of Indonesian stocks, top 10 net‑sell losers listed Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp1.58 trillion in Indonesian equities from 10‑14 August 2026, with the biggest losers being PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp951.1 billion), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (Rp766.8 billion), PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (Rp455.7 billion), PT Astra International Tbk (Rp290.4 billion), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (Rp238.7 billion), PT Indosat Tbk (Rp118.5 billion), PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp86.4 billion), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (Rp73.4 billion), PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (Rp68.4 billion), PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (Rp66.2 billion), Kalbe Farma (Rp37.8 billion) and Darma Henwa (Rp35.9 billion). title: Astra International posts 22% YoY profit decline in Q2 2026, analysts keep buy recommendation
text: Astra International posts 22% YoY profit decline in Q2 2026, analysts keep buy recommendation PT Astra International Tbk reported net profit of Rp 6.7 trillion in Q2 2026, 22.1% lower YoY and only 39.7% of MNC Sekuritas estimate, indicating performance below expectations. The decline was driven by a Rp 2.4 trillion non‑recurring charge from fair‑value adjustments and impairments in its geothermal and nickel divisions, while the mining solutions segment saw revenue fall 15% YoY and mining profit plunge 88% YoY to Rp 607 billion. Despite the weakness, the automotive and financial services segments grew about 6% YoY, with automotive sales gaining a 51% market share, and the group’s cash‑rich position supported a continued buyback program. Analysts from BRI Danareksa and MNC Sekuritas kept a buy rating on PT Astra International Tbk, setting target prices of Rp 6,850 and Rp 7,000 respectively, and highlighted the subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk as the main weight on earnings but with potential recovery in the second half of 2026.

title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) announces focus on three core profit-generating segments
text: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) announces focus on three core profit-generating segments PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) said it will concentrate development on three core businesses—automotive, financial services, and mining solutions & heavy equipment. These segments currently contribute 40%, 31% and 18% of revenue respectively, with other businesses accounting for 11%. Astra plans to increase its stake in AUTO through a voluntary tender offer at Rp3,600 per share, a transaction that could cost about Rp858 billion, and it approved a share-buyback program of up to Rp8 trillion for the next 12 months; United Tractors (UT) also announced a share-buyback of up to Rp2 trillion for three months. In the latest period, the automotive unit posted net profit of Rp5.9 trillion (+9% YoY), financial services Rp4.6 trillion (+6% YoY), while mining solutions & heavy equipment recorded Rp2.7 trillion, down 46% YoY.

title: Analysts Keep Astra International Bullish Amid Growing Chinese Car Competition
text: Analysts Keep Astra International Bullish Amid Growing Chinese Car Competition The article reports that analysts maintain a bullish outlook on PT Astra International Tbk despite intensified competition from Chinese automobile brands. Bloomberg consensus shows 28 of 33 analysts recommending a buy, with target prices ranging from Rp5,900 to Rp7,500 per share and a consensus target of Rp6,583 for the next 12 months. Astra sustained a 51% share of Indonesia’s four‑wheel wholesale market in the first half of 2026, recording 222,371 units sold—a 10% year‑on‑year increase—while the low‑cost green car segment captured 78% of the national market and 85% in June. Strong demand for hybrid and commercial vehicles, together with a recovering national automotive market, underpins the continued overweight recommendation and its status as a top pick.

title: IHSG jumps over 2% as major banks and state‑owned firms drive the rally
text: IHSG jumps over 2% as major banks and state‑owned firms drive the rally The article explains that Indonesia’s composite index (IHSG) surged more than 2% on Friday, reaching 5,881 points after opening at 5,806.17 points. The rally was led by large‑cap banks—Bank Central Asia adding 13.27 points, Bank Mandiri 9 points, Bank Rakyat Indonesia 4.39 points and Bank Negara Indonesia 2.98 points—along with the top‑trading stocks BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, BRPT and TPIA. Conglomerate issuers AMMN, BREN and DCII, as well as Astra International and state‑owned enterprises Aneka Tambang and Telkom Indonesia each contributed roughly 3–6 index points to the gain. The move occurred amid a market‑wide advance in utilities, raw‑material, financial and technology sectors, with total transaction value of about Rp 2.59 trillion and 5.57 billion shares traded in 358 k transactions.

title: IHSG Edges Higher, Review Today's Stock Recommendations
text: IHSG Edges Higher, Review Today's Stock Recommendations The Indonesian Composite Index (IHSG) closed at 6,236.13 on 31 July 2026, up 0.80%, driven by gains in BBRI, ASII and AMMN while declines in BBCA, TLKM and ADRO limited the advance. Ten of eleven sectors posted green performance, led by Basic Industry (+2.54%) and with Non‑Cyclical slipping 0.03%, as foreign investors recorded net sells of Rp34.82 billion in the regular market and Rp250.53 billion across all markets. The market also noted the upcoming rebalancing of the IDX30, LQ45 and IDX80 indices effective 3 August to 30 October 2026, which could boost trading in newly added constituents, while ETF EIDO and MSCI Indonesia activity remained modest. Separate corporate updates disclosed that DRMA targets a 10 % sales increase in 2026 after reporting H1 sales of Rp3.16 trillion (+13.82% YoY), SMRA posted H1 marketing sales of Rp1.20 trillion (+37% YoY) and aims for Rp5.20 trillion in 2026, and ELSA announced a buyback program of up to Rp100 billion scheduled from 3 August to 2 November 2026 following a 29.19 % profit rise to Rp434.71 billion.
